text: **Application of usability engineering to medical devices**

table_body:
EN 62366-1: 2015+A1:2020

Clause

Requirement + Test

Result - Remark

Verdict

4

General requirements

P

4.1

USABILITY ENGINEERING PROCESS

4.1.1

The MANUFACTURER shall establish, document, implement and maintain a USABILITY ENGINEERING PROCESS, as defined in Clause 5, to provide SAFETY for the PATIENT USER and others. The PROCESS shall address USER interactions with the MEDICAL DEVICE according to the ACCOMPANYING DOCUMENTATION.

Usability engineering file (document no. CE-PT9L-12, version 1.0)

User guide (document no. PT9L-SMSY01, version 1.0)

P

USABILITY ENGINEERING activities for a MEDICAL DEVICE shall be planned, carried out, and documented by personnel competent on the basis of appropriate education, training, skills or experience.

ISO 13485:2016 complied.

(document no.SX 2095583-1)

Section 1.2 of Usability engineering file (document no. CE-PT9L-12, version 1.0)

P

Where a documented product realization PROCESS exists, such as that described in Clause 7 of ISO 13485:2016, it shall incorporate the appropriate parts of or reference the USABILITY ENGINEERING PROCESS.

ISO 13485:2016 complied.

(document No.SX 2095583-1)

P

A depiction of the interrelationship between the RISK MANAGEMENT PROCESS of ISO 14971:2019 and the USABILITY ENGINEERING PROCESS described in this standard is shown in Figure A.5.

ISO 14971: 2019 complied

Document No.:PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0

P

The activities described in Clause 5, as shown Figure A.5, are described in a logical order, but they may be carried out in a flexible order as appropriate.

See usability engineering file (document no. CE-PT9L-12, version 1.0)

P

4.1.2

RISK CONTROL as it relates to USER INTERACE design

P

To reduce use-related RISK, the MANUFACTURER shall use one or more of the following options, in the priority listed

Complied by inspection of Usability engineering file (document no. CE-PT9L-12, version 1.0)

P

a) inherent safe design and manufacture

inherent safe design and manufacture complied

P

b) protective measures in the MEDICAL DEVICE itself or in the manufacturing PROCESS; and

N/A

c) information for SAFETY and, where appropriate, training to USERS.

Instruction for use provided for users

P

4.1.3

Information for SAFETY as it relates to USABILITY

When, in accordance with the priorities of 4.1.2, information for SAFETY is used as a RISK CONTROL measure, the MANUFACTURER shall subject this information to the USABILITY ENGINEERING PROCESS to determine that the information

See usability engineering file (document no. CE-PT9L-12, version 1.0) and User guide (document no. PT9L-SMSY01, version 1.0)

P

– is perceivable by,

–is understandable to, and

– supports CORRECT USE of the MEDICAL DEVICE by

P

USERS of the intended USER PROFILES in the context of the intended USE ENVIRONMENT.

P

Conscious disregard of such information for SAFETY by the USER is considered to be an intentional act or intentional omission of an act that is counter to or violates NORMAL USE and is also beyond any further reasonable means of USER INTERFACE-related RISK CONTROL by the

MANUFACTURER (i.e. ABNORMAL USE).

P

4.2

USABILITY ENGINEERING FILE

P

The results of the USABILITY ENGINEERING PROCESS shall be stored in the USABILITY ENGINEERING FILE. The RECORDS and other documents that form the USABILITY ENGINEERING FILE may form part of other documents and files.

see section 1.3 of Usability Engineering File (document no. CE-PT9L-12, version 1.0)

P

4.3

Tailoring of the USABILITY ENGINEERING effort

P

The level of effort and the choice of methods and tools used to perform the USABILITY ENGINEERING PROCESS may vary based on:

See section 1.4 of Usability engineering file (document no. CE-PT9L-12, version 1.0)

P

a) the size and COMPLEXITY of the USER INTERFACE;

P

b) the SEVERITY of the HARM associated with the use of the MEDICAL DEVICE;

P

c) the extent or complexity of the USE SPECIFICATION;

P

d) the presence of USER INTERFACE OF UNKNOWN PROVENANCE; and

P

e) the extent of the modification to an existing MEDICAL DEVICE USER INTERFACE that had been subjected to the USABILITY ENGINEERING PROCESS.

The usability engineering process performed.

N/A

5

USABILITY ENGINEERING PROCESS

P

5.1

Prepare USE SPECIFICATION

P

The MANUFACTURER shall prepare a USE SPECIFICATION. The USE SPECIFICATION shall include:

Described in section 2.1 in Usability Engineering File (document no. CE-PT9L-12)

P

– intended medical indication;

P

– intended PATIENT population;

P

– intended part of the body or type of tissue applied to or interacted with;

P

– intended USER PROFILE;

P

– USE ENVIRONMENT; and

P

– operating principle.

P

5.2

Identify USER INTERFACE characteristics related to SAFETY and potential USE ERRORS

P

The MANUFACTURER shall identify USER INTERFACE characteristics that could be related to SAFETY as part of a RISK ANALYSIS performed according to ISO 14971:2019, 5.3.

see section 3.1.2 of the Usability engineering file (document no. CE-PT9L-12, version 1.0)

P

This identification may also be performed using the tools and techniques from the USABILITY ENGINEERING PROCESS.

see section 3.1 of the Usability engineering file (document no. CE-PT9L-12, version 1.0)

P

This identification shall include consideration of the PRIMARY OPERATING FUNCTIONS that are provided in applicable particular MEDICAL DEVICE SAFETY standards.

see section 3.1.1 of the Usability engineering file (document no. CE-PT9L-12, version 1.0)

P

Based on the identified USER INTERFACE characteristics and USE SPECIFICATION, the MANUFACTURER shall identify the USE ERRORS that could occur and are related to the USER INTERFACE. This identification may be accomplished by conducting a TASK analysis.

see section 3.1.3 of the Usability engineering file (document no. CE-PT9L-12, version 1.0)

P

The results of this identification of characteristics related to SAFETY and potential USE ERRORS shall be stored in the USABILITY ENGINEERING FILE.

See Usability Engineering File (document no. CE-PT9L-12)

P

5.3

Identify known or foreseeable HAZARDS and HAZARDOUS SITUATIONS

See section 4.1 of the Usability Engineering File (document no. CE-PT9L-12)

P

The MANUFACTURER shall identify known or foreseeable HAZARDS and HAZARDOUS SITUATIONS, which could affect PATIENTS, USERS or others, related to use of the MEDICAL DEVICE.

See attached Table 5.3

P

This identification shall be conducted as part of a RISK ANALYSIS performed according to ISO 14971:2019, 5.4.

See risk management report in PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0

During the identification of HAZARDS and HAZARDOUS SITUATIONS, the following shall be considered:

P

– USE SPECIFICATION, including USER PROFILE(S) (see 5.1);

Considered

P

– information on HAZARDS and HAZARDOUS SITUATIONS known for existing USER INTERFACES of MEDICAL DEVICES of a similar type, if available; and

N/A

– identified USE ERRORS (see 5.2).

Complied

P

The results of this identification of HAZARDS and HAZARDOUS SITUATIONS shall be stored in the USABILITY ENGINEERING FILE.

Complied

P

5.4

Identify and describe HAZARD-RELATED USE SCENARIOS

See section 5.1 of Usability Engineering File (document no. CE-PT9L-12)

P

The MANUFACTURER shall identify and describe the reasonably foreseeable HAZARD-RELATED USE SCENARIOS associated with the identified HAZARDS and HAZARDOUS SITUATIONS.

See attached Table 5.4

P

The description of each identified HAZARD-RELATED USE SCENARIO shall include all TASKS and their sequences as well as the SEVERITY of the associated HARM.

See section 5.1 of Usability Engineering File (document no. CE-PT9L-12)

P

5.5

Select the HAZARD-RELATED USE SCENARIOS for SUMMATIVE EVALUATION

P

The MANUFACTURER shall select the HAZARD-RELATED USE SCENARIOS to be included in the SUMMATIVE EVALUATION.

See attached Table 5.5

P

The MANUFACTURER shall select:

See section 5.2 of Usability Engineering File (document no. CE-PT9L-12)

P

- all HAZARD -RELATED USE SCENARIOS ;

P

- a subset of the HAZARD-RELATED USE SCENARIOS based on the SEVERITY of the potential HARM that could be caused by USE ERROR (e.g. for which medical intervention would be needed); or

P

a subset of the HAZARD -RELATED USE SCENARIOS based on the SEVERITY of the potential HARM and based on other circumstances specific to the MEDICAL DEVICE and the MANUFACTURER

P

A summary of any selection scheme, the rationale for its use and the results of applying it shall be stored in the USABILITY ENGINEERING FILE.

See section 4.1 of Usability Engineering File (document no. CE-PT9L-12)

P

5.6

Establish USER INTERFACE SPECIFICATION

P

The MANUFACTURER shall establish and maintain a USER INTERFACE SPECIFICATION.

See attached Table 5.6

P

The USERINTERFACE SPECIFICATION shall consider:

See section 5.3 of Usability Engineering File (document no. CE-PT9L-12)

- the USE SPECIFICATION (see 5.1);

- the known or foreseeable USE ERRORS associated with the MEDICAL DEVICE (see 5.2); and

- the HAZARD -RELATED USE SCENARIOS (see 5.4)

The USER INTERFACE SPECIFICATION shall include:

See section 5.3 of Usability Engineering File (document no. CE-PT9L-12)

- testable technical requirements relevant to the USER INTERFACE, including the requirements for those parts of the USER INTERFACE associated with the selected RISK CONTROL measures;

- an indication as to whether ACCOMPANYING DOCUMENTATION is required; and

- an indication as to whether MEDICAL DEVICE -specific training is required.

The USER INTERFACE SPECIFICATION shall be stored in the USABILITY ENGINEERING FILE. The USER INTERFACE SPECIFICATION may be integrated into other specifications.

See Usability Engineering File (document no. CE-PT9L-12)

P

5.7

Establish USER INTERFACE EVALUATION plan

P

5.7.1

General

P

The MANUFACTURER shall establish and maintain a USER INTERFACE EVALUATION plan for the USER INTERFACE SPECIFICATION.

See section 7 of Usability Engineering File (document no. CE-PT9L-12)

P

The USER INTERFACE EVALUATION plan shall

  1. document the objective and identify the method of any planned FORMATIVE EVALUATIONS and SUMMATIVE EVALUATIONS ;
  1. if USABILITY TESTS are employed,

- document which USER GROUPS are intended to be included in the test;

- document the test environment and other conditions of use, based on the USE SPECIFICATION;

- specify whether ACCOMPANYING DOCUMENTATION is provided during the test;and

- specify whether MEDICAL DEVICE-Specific training is provided prior to the test and the minimum elapsed time between the training and the beginning of the test.

USER INTERFACE EVALUATION methods may be quantitative or qualitative. USER INTERFACE EVALUATION may be performed in a variety of locations, such as, in a laboratory setting, in a simulated USE ENVIRONMENT or in the actual USE ENVIRONMENT.

The USER INTERFACE EVALUATION plan may be integrated into other plans.

The USER INTERFACE EVALUATION plan shall be stored in the USABILITY ENGINEERING FILE.

See Usability Engineering File (document no. CE-PT9L-12)

P

5.7.2

FORMATIVE EVALUATION planning

See attached Table 5.7

P

The USER INTERFACE evaluation plan for FORMATIVE EVALUATION shall address:

See section 7.1 of Usability Engineering File (document no. CE-PT9L-12)

  1. the evaluation methods being used;
  1. which part of the USER INTERFACE is being evaluated;and
  1. when in the USABILITY ENGINEERING PROCESS to perform each of the USER INTERFACE EVALUATIONS

5.7.3

SUMMATIVE EVALUATION planning

See attached Table 5.7

P

For each selected HAZARD -RELATED USE SCENARIO (see 5.5), the USER INTERFACE EVALUATION plan for SUMMATIVE EVALUATION shall specify:

See section 7.2 of Usability Engineering File (document no. CE-PT9L-12)

P

  1. the evaluation method being used and a rationale that the method produces OBJECTIVE EVIDENCE;
  1. Which part of the USER INTERFACE is being evaluated;
  1. where applicable, the criteria for determining whether the information for SAFETY 1Sperceivable, understandable and supports CORRECT USE of the MEDICAL DEVICE (4.1.3):
  1. the availability of the ACCOMPANYING DOCUMENTATION and provision of training during the SUMMATIVE EVALUATION : and
  1. * for a USABILITY TEST,

- how the characteristics of the test participants are representative of the intended PROFILES;

- justifying how the test participants are grouped into distinct USER GROUPS for the purpose of determining the number of test participants;

- the test environment and conditions of use and a rationale for how they are adequately representative of the intended USE ENVIRONMENT;

- the definition of CORRECT USE for each HAZARD -RELATED USE SCENARIO ; and

- the method of collecting data during the USABILITY TEST for the subsequent analysis of observed USE ERRORS and use difficulties.

The SUMMATIVE EVALUATION may be performed in a single evaluation or multiple evaluations.

5.8

Perform USER INTERFACE design, implementation and FORMATIVE EVALUATION

P

The MANUFACTURER shall design and implement the USER INTERFACE, including the

ACCOMPANYING DOCUMENTATION if needed, and training capability, if needed, as described in the USER INTERFACE SPECIFICATION.

See section 6 and section 8 of Usability Engineering File (document no. CE-PT9L-12)

P

The MANUFACTURER shall utilize, as appropriate, USABILITY ENGINEERING methods and techniques, including FORMATIVE EVALUATION to accomplish this design and implementation.

Considered

P

The results of the utilized FORMATIVE EVALUATION shall be stored in the USABILITY ENGINEERING FILE.

Complied

P

Where new USE ERRORS, HAZARDS, HAZARDOUS SITUATIONS or HAZARD-RELATED USE SCENARIOS are discovered during this step, the MANUFACTURER shall repeat the steps of Clause 5 as appropriate.

No new use error or hazardous

N/A

If training on the specific MEDICAL DEVICE is required for the safe use of the MEDICAL DEVICE by the intended USER, the MANUFACTURER shall design and implement a training capability for the EXPECTED SERVICE LIFE of the MEDICAL DEVICE by doing at least one of the following:

Training is not required

N/A

– provide the materials necessary for training;

N/A

– ensure that the materials necessary for training are available;

N/A

– make the training available; or

N/A

– make training available to the RESPONSIBLE ORGANIZATION that enables it to train its USERS.

N/A

5.9

Perform SUMMATIVE EVALUATION of the USABILITY of the USER INTERFACE

P

Upon completion of the design and implementation of the USER INTERFACE, the MANUFACTURER shall perform a SUMMATIVE EVALUATION of each HAZARD-RELATED USE SCENARIO selected in 5.5 on the final or production equivalent USER INTERFACE according to the USER INTERFACE EVALUATION plan.

See section 9 of Usability Engineering File (document no. CE-PT9L-12)

P

For SUMMATIVE EVALUATION, the MANUFACTURER may use data obtained from the SUMMATIVE EVALUATIONS of products with an equivalent USER INTERFACE together with a technical rationale for how this data is applicable.

Considered

Such information described in chapter “Usability validation plan and report” of usability engineering file (document no. CE-PT9L-12, version 1.0)

P

The results shall be stored in the USABILITY ENGINEERING FILE.

Complied

P

The MANUFACTURER shall analyse the data of the SUMMATIVE EVALUATION and shall identify all USE ERRORS and use difficulties that occurred, If a USE ERROR or use difficulty can lead to a HAZARDOUS SITUATION, the root cause of any such USE ERROR or use difficulty shall be determined.

The root causes should be determined based on methods including observations of USER performance as well as subjective comments from the USER.

If new USE ERRORS, HAZARDS, HAZARDOUS SITUATIONS or HAZARD-RELATED USE SCENARIOS are discovered during this data analysis:

- if yes, then the MANUFACTURER shall repeat the activities of Clause 5 as appropriate;

- if not, the MANUFACTURER shall determine whether further improvement of the USERINTERFACE design as it relates to SAFETY is necessary and practicable.

1) if yes, then the MANUFACTURER shall re-enter the USABILITY ENGINEERING PROCESS at5.6:

2) if not.then the MANUFACTURER shall:

  1. document why improvement is not necessary or not practicable;
  1. identify the data from the USABILITY ENGINEERING PROCESS needed to determine the RESIDUAL RISK related to use: and
  1. RESIDUAL RISK according to ISO 14971:2019, 7.3

If the USABILITY ENGINEERING PROCESS detailed in this International Standard has been complied with, then the USABILITY of a MEDICAL DEVICE as it relates to SAFETY is presumed to be acceptable, unless there is OBJECTIVE EVIDENCE to the contrary.

Considered

P

5.10

USER INTERFACE OF UNKNOWN PROVENANCE

Not used of unknown provenance

N/A

Instead of all the requirements of 5.1 through 5.9, UOUP may be evaluated according to Annex C.

N/A

Annex C

Evaluation of a USER INTERFACE OF UNKNOWN PROVENANCE (UOUP)

N/A

C.2.1

USER SPECIFICATION

The MANUFACTURER established an application specification as required in 5.1. The MANUFACTURER shall store this USER SPECIFICATION in the USABILITY ENGINEERING FILE.

No such conditon

N/A

C.2.2

Review of POST-PRODUCTION information

The MANUFACTURER of the MEDICAL DEVICE with UOUP shall review available POST-PRODUCTION information including complaints and field reports for incidents or near incidents.

N/A

All identified cases of USE ERROR that could result in a HAZARDOUS SITUATION or those cases where field information suggests HAZARDS or HAZARDOUS SITUATIONS that could have been caused by inadequate USABILITY shall be stored in the USABILITY ENGINEERING FILE and addressed in C.2.3 and C.2.4.

N/A

C.2.3

HAZARDS AND HAZARDOUS SITUATIONS related to USABILITY

The MANUFACTURER shall review the RISK ANALYSIS of the MEDICAL DEVICE with UOUP and ensure that the HAZARDS and HAZARDOUS SITUATIONS associated with USABILITY have been identified and documented.

N/A

C.2.4

RISK CONTROL

The MANUFACTURER shall verify and document that adequate RISK CONTROL measures have been implemented for all identified HAZARDS and HAZARDOUS SITUATIONS identified in C.2.3 and that all RISKS are reduced to an acceptable level as indicated by the RISK ASSESSMENT.

N/A

If the MANUFACTURER determines that changes to any part of the USER INTERFACE are required to reduce RISK to an acceptable level, those changes shall not be considered UOUP and shall be subject to the requirements of 5.1 through 5.9.

N/A

C.2.5

RESIDUAL RISK evaluation

Based on any new information identified in performing steps C.2.3 and C.2.4, the

MANUFACTURER shall re-evaluate the overall RESIDUAL RISK according to ISO 14971:2019, 7.3, and document the result in either the USABILITY ENGINEERING FILE or the RISK MANAGEMENT FILE.

N/A
